statements.text: Senator Wyden and I are asking federal agencies for information on how they utilize AI, and what steps they are taking to ensure the technology is used appropriately. https://t.co/Nq3tRYKbC3

As technological innovations such as artificial intelligence are used more frequently by government agencies, it is important for Congress to gain a better understanding of AI applications within the Finance Committee’s jurisdiction.

AI offers seemingly endless opportunities for every part of American life, including health care. Rather than legislate first and ask questions later, Congress needs to gain a better understanding of AI and carefully consider regulations moving forward. https://t.co/tEPrLkk3BK

Rather than legislate first and ask questions later, Congress needs to build a better understanding of how AI operates in specific contexts, including health care. Our witnesses will identify areas where current policies can adapt effectively, as well as where they fall short.
statements.venue: Senate Finance Committee hearing opening statement on AI in health care

statements.text: Along these lines, AI highlights the need for adaptability. One-size-fits-all, overly rigid, and unduly bureaucratic laws and regulations risk stifling life-saving advances and becoming outdated before they are even codified.
statements.venue: Senate Finance Committee hearing opening statement on AI in health care

statements.text: As America leads the global race in AI innovation, we must ensure our development outpaces competitors like China without compromising citizen privacy or electrical grid reliability. https://t.co/sXh8VQa9is

The U.S. must remain globally competitive in the advancement of artificial intelligence, which requires supporting the infrastructure and energy resources necessary for this growing technology. However, those costs should not be borne by Idaho ratepayers and communities. Large-load customers, such as data centers, should be responsible for the infrastructure and resources needed to power and maintain their facilities.
statements.venue: Press release on Ratepayer Protection Act vote

statements.text: America must lead the world in artificial intelligence, but everyday families should not have to pay for the massive power grids and infrastructure required by big tech data centers.  I voted to advance the Ratepayer Protection Act to ensure large-load customers pay their fair share for energy upgrades, keeping electricity bills affordable for Idaho families and local businesses.  We can power American innovation while still protecting working families from bearing the cost.  It’s unfortunate Senate Democrats failed to join us in advancing this important bill the House had already passed 417-3. https://t.co/KgD6ORdGKX
